reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every function f from the real line to the real numbers, if f is twice continuously differentiable and the closure of its nonzero support is compact, let gamma be the mean-zero, variance-one Gaussian probability measure on the real line. Set m = integral f(x)^2 d gamma(x). Then
integral f(x)^2 log(f(x)^2) d gamma(x) - m log(m) <= 2 integral (f prime(x))^2 d gamma(x).
All integrals are real Bochner integrals over the whole real line; f prime is the real derivative. The logarithm is the totalized real logarithm, so zero arguments are allowed and 0 log(0) contributes zero. The quantifier includes signed functions and the identically zero function, with no positivity or nonzero-mass restriction. In particular, if m = 0, the term m log(m) is zero and the displayed expression remains defined. No normalization m = 1 is assumed. The left side is the homogeneous entropy expression for f squared with its mass subtraction; no normalized-density or Kullback-Leibler identification is asserted. The coefficient on derivative energy is exactly 2 and is independent of f.
objects: A real-valued function f; its real derivative f prime; the Gaussian measure gamma = gaussianReal 0 1; the nonnegative mass m = integral f squared d gamma; the displayed homogeneous entropy expression; the squared-derivative energy.
domains: f has domain and codomain the real numbers. gamma is a probability measure on the real line with its canonical Borel structure. Every integral is over the entire real line and is a real Bochner integral.
quantifiers: For every f : real numbers -> real numbers, and for every proof that f is C2 and every proof that f has compact support, the displayed inequality holds. gamma is locally fixed by the let expression as the mean-zero, variance-one Gaussian; it is not universally quantified. The notation m merely abbreviates the mass integral.
assumptions: Exactly two caller analytic assumptions: f is twice continuously differentiable and the closure of its nonzero support is compact. Signed functions and the zero function are permitted. There is no positivity, normalization, positive-mass, integrability, distributional-law, inequality, or limit-certificate premise.
conclusion: integral f(x)^2 log(f(x)^2) d gamma(x) - (integral f(x)^2 d gamma(x)) log(integral f(x)^2 d gamma(x)) <= 2 integral (f prime(x))^2 d gamma(x).
scopes: The C2 and compact-support assumptions concern f on the whole real line. Every logarithm of a square and every logarithm of the mass uses the totalized real logarithm. Zero-square and zero-mass products are zero. No normalized-density/KL conclusion is included; for arbitrary mass the entropy is the displayed homogeneous expression.
constant_dependencies: The derivative-energy coefficient is exactly 2. The Gaussian parameters are fixed mean 0 and variance 1. These constants do not depend on f, its sign, support, mass, or normalization.
